q: The open mapping theorem states that a surjective bounded linear operator T: X → Y between Banach spaces maps open sets to open sets. A corollary is:
opts: If T is bijective and bounded, then T⁻¹ is also bounded (bounded inverse theorem)
exp: Bounded inverse theorem (corollary of open mapping): if T: X → Y is a bounded bijection between Banach spaces, T⁻¹ is automatically bounded. This is used constantly: e.g., if a Banach space has two complete norms, and one is finer, they must be equivalent.
